name: Isolated Tetra-Amelia Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Isolated Tetra-Amelia

criteria.description: Complete congenital absence of all four limbs (tetra-amelia)
No associated major internal organ malformations or syndromic features
Identification of pathogenic variants in the WNT3 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of complete absence of all four limbs without other syndromic malformations; genetic confirmation supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; genetic testing for WNT3 mutations can confirm diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Complete congenital absence of all four limbs
searchTerms: no arms or legs present at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absence of both upper and lower extremities from birth
searchTerms: missing both arms and legs since birth
no upper and lower limbs present

common.symptomName: Hypoplastic or absent hands and feet
searchTerms: underdeveloped or missing hands and feet

common.symptomName: Shortened long bones of the limbs (when partially present)

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to chest wall abnormalities
searchTerms: breathing difficulty from chest wall problems
respiratory distress due to chest deformity
problems with sucking or swallowing in infancy

occasional.symptomName: Mild skin hypoplasia over limb stumps
searchTerms: reduced skin thickness on amputated limbs
kidney abnormalities like missing one kidney

laboratory: Genetic testing revealing WNT3 gene mutations
imaging: X-rays showing complete absence of all four limbs
Chest radiographs may show thoracic cage abnormalities
Ultrasound to exclude internal organ malformations
genetic: Pathogenic variants in WNT3 gene (autosomal recessive inheritance)
other: Prenatal ultrasound may detect limb absence

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of proximal limb elements with absent or hypoplastic distal segments
Often associated with thalidomide exposure or other teratogens
Severe body wall defects with limb abnormalities
Associated with visceral malformations and amniotic band sequence

redFlags: Complete absence of all four limbs at birth
Respiratory distress due to thoracic cage abnormalities
Presence of associated major internal organ malformations
references: Kjaer KW, et al. Mutations in WNT3 cause tetra-amelia syndrome. Nat Genet. 2007
